short: Printing, reformation, global voyaging and the scientific revolution.
full:
The Early Modern Period, roughly 1500 to 1760, is characterised by acceleration. Movable-type printing made ideas cheap to reproduce and impossible to suppress, which in turn made the Reformation unstoppable in a way earlier dissent had not been.

European ships reached the Americas, rounded Africa and crossed the Pacific, initiating the Columbian Exchange, colonial empires and the Atlantic slave trade. The Scientific Revolution replaced authority with observation and mathematics as the test of truth. By its close, the modern state — with standing armies, permanent bureaucracies and national debt — was recognisably in place.
